name: logic-programming-skills
description: Agent skills for logic programming: SWI-Prolog, and s(CASP) goal-directed answer set programming with human-readable justifications. Executable code samples are run against a real swipl before release.

plugins.name: dev-prolog
plugins.description: Use when writing, reviewing, refactoring, or designing Prolog code — including facts, rules, queries, recursion, lists, DCGs, constraint logic programming (CLP(FD)), tabling, modules, exceptions, and PlUnit testing in SWI-Prolog or GNU Prolog projects. Covers idiomatic clause design, unification, backtracking, steadfastness, mode and termination reasoning, the four-port debugger, and the purity discipline that keeps a predicate usable in every mode. Fires on Prolog topics even when the user does not say "Prolog" explicitly — e.g. `.pl` / `.pro` files, expert-system rules, ":- " clause syntax, "predicate", "unification", "backtracking", "logic programming", "definite clause grammar", "rule-based reasoning over a knowledge base", or any task whose source of truth is a set of declarative Horn clauses.

plugins.name: dev-scasp
plugins.description: Use when writing, reviewing, or debugging s(CASP) programs — the goal-directed Answer Set Programming system running inside SWI-Prolog via `library(scasp)`. Covers default negation (`not`), classical negation (`-`), abducibles (`#abducible`), integrity constraints (`:- Body.`), even-loop choice construction, predicate annotations (`#pred ... :: '@(X)...'`), the dual program and how unbound variables make it explode, and human-readable justifications. Fires on s(CASP) topics even when the user does not say "s(CASP)" explicitly — e.g. "default reasoning in Prolog", "abductive reasoning", "stable models with Prolog syntax", "integrity constraint over a knowledge base", "expert system with defeasible rules", "explainable rules engine", or any task whose source of truth is a set of Horn-ish rules with default negation and goal-directed ASP semantics.
